`GpuTargetConfig::FromProto` unconditionally overwrote `device_description.name`

Only fall back to `device_description_str` when `device_description.name()` is
empty or `se::DeviceDescription::kUndefinedString`, matching the existing
`runtime_version` fallback directly below it. All other checked-in GPU target
specs either omit `gpu_device_info.name` or set both fields identically, so
their behavior is unchanged.

[XLA:CPU] Lower CPU exp to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Enforce direct `FuncOp` nesting in `NestedInIfrtFuncTrait` and simplify IFRT IR passes

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Enforce direct `FuncOp` nesting in `NestedInIfrtFuncTrait` and simplify IFRT IR passes

Operations carrying `NestedInIfrtFuncTrait` were silently accepted outside any function (such as directly inside a `builtin.module`) because the trait verifier only checked function attributes when an enclosing `func.func` was found. Walking up to any enclosing function via `getParentOfType` also allowed IFRT ops to appear inside nested regions such as `stablehlo.if`.

Tighten `NestedInIfrtFuncTrait` to require the direct parent to be a `func.func` with `ifrt.function` or `ifrt.reshard_function`, rejecting unenclosed and nested-region ops.

Combined with the single-block body invariant on IFRT functions, every IFRT op is now guaranteed to live directly in the entry block of its enclosing IFRT function. Simplify IFRT IR import, compilation, and MPMD conversion passes accordingly:
* Replace function-scoped `.walk` calls (and reverse pre-order walking in `IfrtDcePass`) with direct entry-block scans via `getOps`, and guard `IfrtAddCtrlDependenciesPass` with `IsIfrtFunction` so non-IFRT functions are skipped.
* Replace whole-module `.walk` calls in `IfrtCompileAtomProgramPass`, `IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass`, and `IfrtDuplicatedCalleeEliminationPass` with direct iteration over IFRT functions so outlined atom program bodies are not traversed.
* Replace greedy pattern rewriting and whole-module walking in `IfrtReshardToCopyArraysPass` with direct per-IFRT-function entry-block scans via `mlir::IRRewriter`, failing the pass cleanly when a convertible `ifrt.Reshard` has a used control output.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate element bounds and non-zero product in `xla::ifrt::Index`

`Index` only rejected negative elements inside `Index::FromProto`, leaving direct C++ construction via `Index(elements)` and arithmetic via `operator+`, `operator-`, and `operator*` able to produce negative, overflow-wrapped, or unreachable coordinates whose cumulative non-zero element product exceeds `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (and thus cannot fit inside any valid `Shape`).

Add `Index::Create` returning `absl::InvalidArgumentError` if any element is negative or if the cumulative product of non-zero elements exceeds `Shape::kMaxNumElements`, delegate both `Index(elements)` (via `CHECK_OK`) and `Index::FromProto` to `Index::Create`, and `CHECK` that `Index::Zeros` and `Index` arithmetic operators preserve non-negativity and the non-zero product bound without underflow or overflow. Update `IndexDomain::Intersect` to construct the intersection origin and shape via `Index::Create` and `Shape::Create`, and update `IndexDomainTest.Contains` and `array_slice_impl_test_lib` to avoid constructing `Index` instances with negative coordinates.

[XLA:PjRt] Tighten transpose kernel target gating, unrolling, and helpers

Follow up cleanups to the 512 bit transpose microkernels:

* Match `HWY_AVX3_SPR` with `==` instead of `<=` and guard x86 cache and strip heuristics with `HWY_ARCH_X86`. `HWY_AVX10_2` and future 64 byte non x86 targets now default to the 512 bit kernels instead of inheriting SPR workarounds.

* Call `f` directly inside the `ForEachIndexedImpl` fold expression to avoid forwarding `f` across multiple pack elements.

Existing x86 behavior up to `HWY_AVX3_SPR` is unchanged.

* `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/pjrt:transpose_kernels_test` verifies all microkernel and macrokernel shapes and stride branches across generated Highway targets.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Verify devices, memory kind, and per-shard byte size for `io_aliases`

Aliasing an input to an output on `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` requires the two buffers to reside on the same devices and memory kind, while allowing different element types, per-shard shapes, and layouts as long as their per-shard on-device byte size matches. Enforcing only element-type and per-shard-shape equality missed impossible cross-device and host-to-device aliases while rejecting valid bitcast-style or layout-changing aliases.

`IfrtCallOpInterface` verification now requires matching devices and effective memory kind on every `io_aliases` pair (normalizing omitted and explicit `"device"` memory kinds), and drops the element-type and per-shard-shape requirements. When both sides have user-specified layouts or both have default layouts (treating an omitted `layout` attribute as default), verification checks per-shard byte-size equality via `xla::ShapeUtil::ArraySize` (rejecting unsizable element types or invalid layouts cleanly); `auto` layouts skip the check because layout selection is deferred to the compiler, and mixed default/user-specified pairs skip it because default-layout padding is target-dependent.

Also updates `ProgramInterpreter` to use `GetDonatedOrAliasedInputIndices` instead of unpacking raw `io_aliases` attributes.

[IFRT IR] Tighten IFRT IR op verifiers and factor shared checks onto op interfaces

Several IFRT IR operations left structural and type invariants unverified or duplicated across per-op verifiers: `ifrt.BitcastArrays` allowed non-donated inputs, `auto` layouts, and distinct device lists of equal length; `ifrt.Assemble` and `ifrt.Disassemble` omitted per-shard dtype, memory kind, layout, and local shape checks; `ifrt.RemapArrays` only rejected `auto` layouts on mapped inputs while letting unmapped `auto`-layout inputs pass; `ifrt.After` accepted zero inputs; and `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` left `arg_attrs` and `res_attrs` arity unverified.

This lets downstream passes (`IfrtCallDedupPass`, `IfrtDcePass`, `IfrtMergeOpsPass`) and `ProgramMemoryTracer` drop redundant emptiness, uniform-device, and bounds guards.

Tighten `ifrt.BitcastArrays` to require `donated = true`, concrete layouts, and identical `IfrtDevicesAttr` placement; unify concrete-layout and per-shard metadata checks across `ifrt.Assemble`, `ifrt.Disassemble`, and `ifrt.RemapArrays` (checking all `ifrt.RemapArrays` inputs upfront); and require at least one input on `ifrt.After`. display_title: [XLA] Peel bitcasts when checking buffer aliasing in ShouldFuseInPlaceOp

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Peel bitcasts when checking buffer aliasing in ShouldFuseInPlaceOp

`InstructionFusion::ShouldFuseInPlaceOp` compared the in place operand against
sibling consumer operands, the producer, and producer operands by raw pointer.
When a `dynamic-update-slice` updated `bitcast(x)` and its producer read `x`,
or the reverse, fusion added a second parameter for the same buffer. Alias
analysis then rejected in place sharing, so `CopyInsertion` inserted full
buffer copies.

Peel `bitcast` chains (including tuple elements) in
`xla/hlo/transforms/instruction_fusion.cc` and conservatively forbid fusing
when a sibling consumer operand, the producer, or another producer operand
aliases the resolved in place base buffer. Also verify that a fused `slice` or
`dynamic-slice` reads the exact same base operand as the `dynamic-update-slice`
and check all in place operand pairs before allowing fusion. Fusions where the
slice and update share the same operand, shape, and indices remain allowed.

Computations that previously fused reads across a bitcast into an in place
update now keep the read separate and avoid buffer copies.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:instruction_fusion_test` pins bitcast alias rejection,
  copy elimination, sibling bitcast checks, and shared bitcast slice fusion.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [IFRT IR] Enforce direct `FuncOp` nesting in `NestedInIfrtFuncTrait` and simplify IFRT IR passes

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Enforce direct `FuncOp` nesting in `NestedInIfrtFuncTrait` and simplify IFRT IR passes

Operations carrying `NestedInIfrtFuncTrait` were silently accepted outside any function (such as directly inside a `builtin.module`) because the trait verifier only checked function attributes when an enclosing `func.func` was found. Walking up to any enclosing function via `getParentOfType` also allowed IFRT ops to appear inside nested regions such as `stablehlo.if`.

Tighten `NestedInIfrtFuncTrait` to require the direct parent to be a `func.func` with `ifrt.function` or `ifrt.reshard_function`, rejecting unenclosed and nested-region ops.

Combined with the single-block body invariant on IFRT functions, every IFRT op is now guaranteed to live directly in the entry block of its enclosing IFRT function. Simplify IFRT IR import, compilation, and MPMD conversion passes accordingly:
* Replace function-scoped `.walk` calls (and reverse pre-order walking in `IfrtDcePass`) with direct entry-block scans via `getOps`, and guard `IfrtAddCtrlDependenciesPass` with `IsIfrtFunction` so non-IFRT functions are skipped.
* Replace whole-module `.walk` calls in `IfrtCompileAtomProgramPass`, `IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass`, and `IfrtDuplicatedCalleeEliminationPass` with direct iteration over IFRT functions so outlined atom program bodies are not traversed.
* Replace greedy pattern rewriting and whole-module walking in `IfrtReshardToCopyArraysPass` with direct per-IFRT-function entry-block scans via `mlir::IRRewriter`, failing the pass cleanly when a convertible `ifrt.Reshard` has a used control output.
